rationale.1:Tech: Tech districts raise daytime population, commuter inflow, and infrastructure-related service coordination needs.
rationale.2:Social: Social gathering activity increases crowding, nightlife pressure, and incident or complaint likelihood.
rationale.3:Arts: Arts activity contributes event-based surges and venue concentration but is less universal than core demand drivers.
rationale.4:Health: Health and sports activity adds facility load, park use, and periodic safety or traffic management demand.
rationale.5:Education: Education hubs generate recurring peak-time flows and localized public service needs around institutions.
rationale.6:Community: Community-oriented areas often reflect civic engagement, family presence, and direct interaction with public services.
rationale.7:Food: Food and dining clusters strongly correlate with mixed-use intensity, sanitation needs, noise, and footfall pressure.
rationale.8:Diversity: Diversity-related communities can indicate specialized gathering patterns and culturally specific service access needs.
rationale.9:Free-1: This auxiliary channel may capture residual interaction signals linked to unmet service demand patterns.
rationale.10:Free-2: This auxiliary channel may encode additional latent behavior affecting localized management burden.
rationale.11:Global-Structure: Overall mobility, POI density, and land-use structure are the strongest predictors of regional service call intensity.
